web_title: 5. Leading KPIs, Capacity Runway & Management Walk-the-Talk Audit
book_title: Chapter 5: The Operator's Scorecard — KPIs, Capacity & Walk-the-Talk
question: Which 6 leading operational KPIs govern Yash's trajectory, how large is its capacity runway, and has Keyur Shah's management team delivered on past promises?

epigraph.quote: Measure management not by the ambition of its slide deck, but by the gap between last year's timeline and this year's factory floor.
epigraph.author: Governance Underwriting Standard

web_blocks.title: 5.1 Six Leading Operational KPIs to Track

web_blocks.html: Condenser bushings carry 15-to-20-month delivery cycles and multi-year utility approvals. Financial statements therefore lag operational reality. The six leading KPIs below track Yash Highvoltage's real-time momentum:

web_blocks.caption: Yash Highvoltage Leading Operational KPI Dashboard
rows: Provides 15–20 months revenue visibility; watch quarterly book-to-bill >1.0x [1][2].
+40% YoY volume growth in H1 FY27; validates real demand beyond pricing [1].
Halol + Jarod combined capacity doubles unit headroom [1].
Higher RIP mix drives structural gross margin expansion (48.3% in H1 FY27) [1].
Diversifies away from domestic OEM cyclicality; US 27-state push [1][5].
Must stay <75 days as scale doubles; watch receivable days (66d in Sep-26) [2].
web_blocks.takeaway: Every leading indicator moved favorably in H1 FY27, with order book doubling in six months to ₹760 Cr and CCC compressing 18 days to 63 days [1][2].

web_blocks.title: 5.2 Capacity Expansion, Backward Integration & TAM Runway

web_blocks.html: Yash is building a ₹220 crore greenfield RIP/RIS plant at Jarod, Vadodara (2.5 lakh sq. ft. land; 1.5 lakh sq. ft. built-up) [1][2]. By September 30, 2026, it had spent ₹106 crore, with ₹114 crore slated over the next 12 months [1][2]. Combined capacity across Halol (Unit-1) and Jarod (Unit-2) reaches 15,000 units by end-CY26, adding ~6,000 RIP/RIS units yearly [1]. Phase 1 assembly using imported cores issued its first Jarod invoice in H1 FY27 [1]. The IMPL winding machine is running, and the Menzel line is commissioning for Q3 FY27 [1].

In June 2026, Yash also raised ₹151 crore via equity (₹91 Cr) and warrants (₹60 Cr, 25% paid upfront) [1]. Those funds back Phase 2 indigenous RIP/RIS cores up to 550 kV (₹80 Cr capex, ₹36.75 Cr working capital, ₹30 Cr GCP) [1]. Management guides for 3x–4x revenue potential over five years at full scale [1]. A ₹760 crore order book and 27-state US sales coverage support that growth [1][5].
An objective audit of Chairman & MD Keyur Shah and Executive Director (Finance) Darshan Thakkar reveals strong commercial execution alongside two areas where timelines shifted or require monitoring:

web_blocks.caption: Management Walk-the-Talk Audit (Promises vs. Verified Delivery)
rows: Localize dry RIP/RIS & scale to 245 kV
Launched 245 kV RIP (2020) & OIP (2022); RIP now 86% of revenue [1].
US IEEE market entry & seismic qualification
Yash HV USA Inc. live; 27 US states covered; 138/230 kV IEEE seismic passed [1][5].
Swung from ₹2.19 Cr FY26 loss to ₹55 lakh PAT in H1 FY27 within 9 months [1][2].
First assembly invoice issued H1 FY27; full end-to-end core commissioning slated Q3/H2 FY27 [1][3].
FY26 CFO lagged (₹8.82 Cr) on inventory build, but H1 FY27 CFO rebounded to ₹45.2 Cr [1].
web_blocks.takeaway: Management has delivered on technical qualifications, US expansion, and Sukrut turnaround; investors should monitor Q3/H2 FY27 full RIP-core commissioning and export ramp-up.

web_blocks.title: 5.4 Medium-Term TAM Runway & Order-Book Conversion Mechanics

web_blocks.html: India's transformer market should grow from $3.0 billion in 2025 to $4.47 billion by 2030, an 8.33% CAGR [1]. Meanwhile, US power transformer demand is up 119% since 2019, with 100 GW of new peak load needed by 2030 [1]. This addressable demand extends well past Yash's ₹389 crore annualized run-rate [1]. Its ₹760 crore order book on September 30, 2026—nearly double the ₹400 crore backlog in March—gives 15 to 20 months of visibility [1][2].

Management guides for ~4x asset turnover on incremental greenfield capex once Jarod hits full utilization [1]. Yash has already spent ₹106 crore of the ₹220 crore Jarod outlay, with ₹114 crore left over 12 months [1][2]. It has therefore pre-funded the physical capacity for its 3x–4x five-year revenue goal. No major new greenfield capex should be needed in FY28–FY29 [1][2].

The Sukrut Electric joint venture adds a second growth lever in Pune [1][2]. Acquired 50:50 with Quality Power in December 2025, Sukrut swung from a ₹2.19 crore FY26 loss to a ₹55 lakh profit in H1 FY27 [1][2]. As Sukrut scales alongside Jarod, Yash gains complementary manufacturing capacity without diluting management focus.

book_paragraphs: When you and I track a fast-growing industrial company, reported earnings tell us what happened twelve months ago. To know where the business is heading twelve months from now, we need a dashboard of leading operational indicators.

At Yash Highvoltage, six numbers tell the whole story. First, the order book: it stood at ₹150 crore in March 2025, climbed to ₹400 crore in March 2026, and surged to ₹760 crore by September 2026—giving fifteen to twenty months of execution visibility. Second, physical volume: Yash sold 7,272 bushings in FY26 and roughly 4,000 units in just the first half of FY27, a 40% year-on-year volume jump. This is not merely price inflation; more bushings are leaving the factory floor.

Third and fourth are mix shifts: RIP bushings sit at 86% of product revenue, while Exports plus Repair & Services climbed from 9% to 14% of channel revenue in H1 FY27. Fifth is installed capacity, which is doubling from roughly 7,000 units to 15,000 units across Halol and Jarod. Sixth is the cash conversion cycle, which tightened from 81 days in FY26 to 63 days in H1 FY27.

book_subsections.title: Grading Keyur Shah's Walk-the-Talk Record
paragraphs: How has management's execution measured up against its promises? Honestly, the scorecard is impressive, with two caveats worth watching. Keyur Shah promised to climb the voltage curve to 245 kV, break into the US IEEE market, and turn around the Pune-based Sukrut Electric joint venture. Every one of those happened: Yash passed seismic qualification on 138 kV and 230 kV IEEE bushings, signed representation across 27 US states, and swung Sukrut from a ₹2.19 crore loss to a ₹55 lakh profit in nine months.

Where should you keep a skeptical eye? First, full end-to-end indigenous RIP core manufacturing at Jarod is commissioning in Q3/H2 FY27—slightly later than early post-IPO hopes, though assembly with imported cores has already begun invoicing. Second, exports are still only 6% of revenue; the real test of Yash's US and European groundwork will be whether export share breaks into double digits once 550 kV and indigenous RIP cores go live in FY28.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Notice Keyur Shah's restraint on the H1 FY27 call: when an analyst pushed him to guide for 35% EBITDA margins after core integration, he declined to make tall commitments. Under-promising on margins while delivering 28.1% is a healthy cultural sign.

book_subsections.title: What to Watch Quarter by Quarter Over the Next 18 Months
paragraphs: If you are tracking Yash Highvoltage over FY27 and FY28, your checklist is remarkably concrete. First, watch for the formal announcement that end-to-end indigenous RIP/RIS core winding and impregnation at Jarod has moved from trial runs into full commercial production during Q3/H2 FY27. That single milestone enables both lower unit costs and RIP export eligibility.

Second, watch the order book and quarterly book-to-bill ratio. At ₹760 crore in September 2026, Yash has more than 1.9x its annualized H1 revenue sitting in backlog; sustaining quarterly order inflows above ₹180–200 crore will confirm that the US 27-state network and domestic utility tenders are refilling the pipe as execution accelerates.

Third, watch receivable days and inventory turns. Management brought the cash conversion cycle down to 63 days in H1 FY27 even as revenue nearly doubled. Keeping CCC below 70 days while exports scale will prove that growth is self-funding.
